candidates.title: SRET that stays in S-mode clears mstatus.MPRV without flushing the read/write TLB: a machine configured to start outside M-mode with MPRV=1 keeps translations made under the old effective privilege
candidates.component: Interpreter (src/interpret.cpp execute_SRET), shared by native run, the uarch program, the collectors and the log producers; machine creation from configuration (processor.registers written raw, src/machine.cpp init_processor)
candidates.role: Honest operator (transition function); the deviation is identical on every path
candidates.location: src/interpret.cpp execute_SRET (2800-2828): clears MSTATUS_MPRV when spp < PRV_M, then only calls set_prv (which flushes) if prv != spp. Compare execute_MRET (2850-2862) and raise_exception (496-505), which flush TLB_READ/TLB_WRITE when the effective data privilege changes while the privilege mode does not, and write_csr_mstatus (2331-2338). src/translate-virtual-address.hpp 118-123 applies MPRV in every privilege mode. src/machine.cpp init_processor (~179) stores processor.registers.iprv and mstatus without checking the combination.
candidates.description: The read and write TLB sets are not tagged with the effective data privilege (MPRV ? MPP : iprv), so every change of it must flush them. The interpreter does this on mstatus writes, on traps taken M->M with MPRV set, and on MRET that returns to M with MPRV set. execute_SRET misses one case: SRET executed in S-mode with SPP=S while mstatus.MPRV=1. The instruction clears MPRV (correct, privileged spec: an xRET to a mode less privileged than M sets MPRV=0), so the effective data privilege changes from MPP to S, but because prv == spp no flush happens. Entries filled under privilege MPP stay valid: for MPP=U, S-mode then reads and writes U pages with SUM=0 through TLB hits, and a page walk would raise a page fault. The staleness is not architectural (the spec makes MPRV/SUM/privilege changes take effect immediately) although it is the same on native, uarch and collectors. The state MPRV=1 outside M-mode cannot be produced by execution from reset (MRET and SRET leaving M clear MPRV, traps never lower the privilege), but machine creation accepts it from the configuration: processor.registers.iprv=1 with mstatus.MPRV=1 is stored as given and honored by the page walker.
candidates.trigger: Whoever builds the template: a configuration (or a processor backing image) with iprv = S (or U followed by a trap to S) and mstatus.MPRV=1, MPP=U. The guest then executes SRET with SPP=S. No input sender can create the state in a machine that started in M-mode.
candidates.reachability: Not reachable by any input sequence from a machine whose registers hold a combination the privileged specification allows: MPRV is only writable in M-mode (write_csr_mstatus; SSTATUS_W_MASK excludes it), MRET clears it when MPP != M, SRET executed in M always lowers the privilege and clears it, and traps never go from M to S/U. It is reachable only when the template itself is created with iprv != M and MPRV=1, which the emulator accepts (no legalization of the pair). Whether such a template is a valid template depends on reading 'Its registers hold only values that the RISC-V specification and the manual allow for them' per register (then valid: both values are legal individually) or jointly (then not valid).
rating_steps: 1 Out of scope: not excluded by the list. The trigger is the configuration the machine is created from, not 'a deliberate state change made through the machine API', and no snapshot the emulator did not write is involved. If triage reads MPRV=1 outside M as a register value the specification does not allow, the template is not a valid template ('Its registers hold only values that the RISC-V specification and the manual allow for them') and the state is unreachable ('A state is unreachable only if no input sequence produces it from any valid template').

2 Role: interpreter = 'Interpreter, state-access layers ... | Honest operator' (AUDIT.md component table); the same code runs natively, in the uarch program and in the collectors, so no path diverges.

3 High/Medium cases: it matches Medium 'An undocumented deterministic deviation, consistent across all paths, in behavior that no correct guest relies on for isolation or data integrity (R7)': a correct guest (firmware, kernel) can never observe MPRV=1 in S-mode on a compliant hart, so it cannot rely on the flush. None of the High cases applies (no divergence between paths, no crash, no memory-safety issue).

4 Critical: only under a literal reading of R7 ('The emulator implements the RISC-V specification ... Address translation and memory permissions ... any deviation lets an input subvert a correct guest, even a deviation that is consistent across all paths') combined with the per-register reading of the valid-template condition. I do not claim it: no input can bring a correct guest into the state.

5 Low: if the state is ruled outside every valid template, no listed case applies (no path divergence, no crash at the unreachable state) and it is 'a real defect that violates no rule or obligation of this model'.
candidates.claimed_severity: Low (preferred: the state needs a template whose registers combine MPRV=1 with iprv != M) / Medium (if a configuration-made S-mode MPRV=1 start state is a valid template: undocumented deterministic deviation consistent across all paths, R7)
candidates.threat_to_goal: None on the goal of section 1 that I can show: every path computes the same hash, and only a template deliberately built in a non-architectural register state exposes the stale translations. It still breaks the subsystem invariant 'a TLB hit returns exactly what a walk would, or the staleness is architectural' (R7, R10 'Stale cached translations are architectural'), and it shows that machine creation accepts register combinations the interpreter's flush logic does not cover.
candidates.evidence: Ran /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-machine-emulator/549e7dd9-06ba-5ccf-8b17-f8cce9526655/scratchpad/campaign/r9/SUBTLB/mprv/test2.lua with two bare-metal guests (mprv/mprv.S, mprv/mprv2.S) on a machine created with processor.registers = {iprv = 1, mstatus = default | SPP | MPRV (MPP=U), satp = Sv39 root in the RAM image}. Guest: ld from a U page (succeeds as effective privilege U and fills the read TLB), SRET to the next instruction with SPP=S (MPRV becomes 0, iprv stays 1), ld from the same U page again. Observed with mprv.bin: the second load succeeds (pc reaches the 'after' loop at 0x80000030, no trap, mstatus.MPRV=0, iprv=1) although S-mode with SUM=0 must take a load page fault. Control mprv2.bin, identical but with sfence.vma before the second load: the load traps (machine leaves S-mode, iprv=3). The configuration was accepted without error.
candidates.test_idea: Create the machine from the configuration above with mprv.bin, run 60 mcycles, and assert that the second load trapped (pc != address of 'after', or mcause/scause == 13 with tval == 0xC0001000). Alternatively assert that machine creation refuses iprv != 3 together with mstatus.MPRV=1. Fails today (the load completes); passes once execute_SRET flushes TLB_READ/TLB_WRITE when it clears MPRV without changing privilege, or once creation rejects the pair.

not_covered: No Medium-or-above candidate found in this subsystem. What I derived and attacked, with results: (1) flush completeness: every writer of iprv (set_prv), satp (write_csr_satp), and of mstatus MPRV/MPP/SUM/MXR (write_csr_mstatus, raise_exception, execute_MRET, execute_SRET) against the dependency of each TLB set (code: iprv, satp; read: effective privilege, satp, SUM, MXR; write: effective privilege, satp, SUM); only the S->S SRET with MPRV=1 case above is missing, at a state execution cannot reach. (2) fetch cache: the invariant 'fetch cache valid => TLB_CODE slot of that page holds the same mapping' holds on every path that writes TLB_CODE (fetch_translate_pc_slow for pc and pc+2, set_prv, satp, sfence.vma) and every status that leaves the cache alive. (3) hot/cold TLB: every writer of the shadow TLB (write_verified_tlb, write_unverified_tlb, full-shadow write_memory, load, replace_memory_range) updates or invalidates the hot slot; shadow_tlb_verify_slot bounds host pointers. (4) write-TLB dirty tracking across run, collect_mcycle_root_hashes, collect_uarch_cycle_root_hashes, run_uarch/reset_uarch, log_step_uarch, store/load, shared load/destroy/reload, replace_memory_range.

Dynamic coverage is one purpose-built bare-metal guest (/tmp/claude-0/-home-user-machine-emulator/549e7dd9-06ba-5ccf-8b17-f8cce9526655/scratchpad/campaign/r9/SUBTLB/tlbfuzz.S, tlbfuzz.c: S-mode fuzz loop under Sv39/Sv48/Bare with two roots, ASID changes and PPN-only satp changes, random leaf and non-leaf PTE rewrites without sfence.vma, megapages, misaligned megapages, reserved PTE bits, SUM/MXR toggles, U-mode excursions, M-mode MPRV probes with MPP/SUM/MXR changes and nested M->M traps, timer and software interrupts, AMO/LR/SC, page-crossing fetches, TLB slot aliasing, upper-half and non-canonical addresses, targets in RAM, rx/tx buffers, PMA table, CLINT, unmapped). It was compared across native run (random chunking), collect_mcycle_root_hashes (every sample), collect_uarch_cycle_root_hashes, run_uarch+reset_uarch, log_step_uarch+log_reset_uarch for whole mcycles, store/load, and shared-directory load/advance/destroy/reload. Runs: 16 guest seeds to completion (1.7-2.0 million mcycles each, about 16-19 thousand comparison windows per seed, about 290 thousand windows in total), 6 of them with a crafted-TLB injection every 15 windows (about 7,450 injections); a shared-directory pass of 1,196 store/load(sharing)/advance/destroy/reload windows; 781 content-preserving replace_memory_range calls (tx buffer and RAM) with live TLB entries over 2,528 windows; per-uarch-cycle hashes of collect_uarch_cycle_root_hashes against run_uarch plus get_root_hash for about 947 thousand uarch cycles (mcycles of up to 17,494 uarch cycles); page-hash-tree-cache sizes 1, 2, 3, 16 and 300; maximum observed 20,697 uarch cycles in one mcycle over 1.68 million mcycles. No mismatch, crash or failed verify_hash_tree. Linux workloads, floating point, PLIC and HTIF yields inside the fuzz stream were not part of it.

Crafted shadow TLB contents (misplaced slots, unaligned vaddr_page/vp_offset, wrong or out-of-range pma_index, non-zero padding, targets in every PMA kind and outside any PMA) were injected through the validated full-shadow write_memory into both machines and through store/load, then compared across the same paths: no divergence. I did not create machines from a hand-made processor backing file at creation time (the load path after store covers the same code), and I did not fuzz crafted PMA tables (creation refuses a PMA table that differs from the configuration).

The regenerated Solidity step and the EVM harness were not run on uarch steps of this guest (write-TLB ecalls, page walks); I only re-read EmulatorCompat.writeTlbECALL and the C++ uarch replay (uarch_replay_state_access::do_write_tlb), which earlier rounds had checked. The C++ replay verified every step of the sampled whole mcycles (method 'l') because log_step_uarch verifies its own log.

record_step/replay_step state accesses (log_step/verify_step, the main-processor step log used for proofs outside the tournament) keep their own TLB handling (touch_page, init_hot_tlb_contents before logging); read only superficially, not tested.

Sv57 (compiled out), hosts other than x86-64 Linux and JSON-RPC remote machines (fork, rebind) were not exercised. The ASan+UBSan build ran one shortened pass only (2,700 windows, 270 crafted-TLB injections, all methods, no sanitizer report).

Worst-case uarch cycles of an mcycle that stacks an interrupt with a flushing instruction at the trap vector (two full TLB flushes, about 2 x 768 slot writes) was estimated by reading at about 4e4 uarch cycles, well below 2^20 - 1; not measured. The known flush-cost issues (R1-R12-2, R1-R8-3, R1-A7-1) were not re-examined.

Observation not reported as a candidate (outside this angle, unverified against the manual): non-shared backing files, including replace_memory_range images, are mapped MAP_PRIVATE rather than copied, so truncating or rewriting such a file while the machine lives kills the process with SIGBUS (seen when my own test reused one temporary file) or may change untouched pages without any dirty mark. It needs an operator-side change of a file the machine depends on.
